-71.06950,42.36200.name: Massachusetts General Hospital Fertility Center
-71.06950,42.36200.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: John C. Petrozza, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

75.59241,31.30804.name: Sarab Healthcare
75.59241,31.30804.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. Operated by Dr. Sarabjeet Singh. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-122.56812,38.10620.name: Buck Institute for Research on Aging
-122.56812,38.10620.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Buck Institute. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-2.99380,53.41018.name: Pall Mall Medical Centre
-2.99380,53.41018.state: Pall Mall Medical Centre, 5, St Paul's Square, Liverpool, L3 9SJ
-2.99380,53.41018.company: Satellite clinic to CREATE Fertility, Manchester
-2.99380,53.41018.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to CREATE Fertility, Manchester. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

2.32232,48.60446.name: Institut de Recherche Biomédicale des Armées (IRBA)
2.32232,48.60446.state: 1 Place Valérie André BP 73 91223 Brétigny sur Orge, France, France
2.32232,48.60446.desc: A BSL4 laboratory, operational. Run by Army Health Service (SSA). It is categorised as a defense laboratory, working on human health. Personnel work in full-body positive-pressure suits with their own air supply. Containment space: 240 SqM. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-77.04500,38.90400.name: Alliance for Regenerative Medicine
-77.04500,38.90400.desc: The cell and gene therapy sector’s trade association, publishing sector financing and pipeline data and lobbying on reimbursement. Its figures are the ones cited in most coverage of how large this field is, and they are compiled by the field about itself.

73.83000,18.51000.name: Serum Institute of India
73.83000,18.51000.desc: The largest vaccine manufacturer in the world by doses, privately owned, supplying a very large share of the vaccines used in low and middle income countries through UNICEF and Gavi. Much of what it makes is recombinant — produced by engineered organisms — including hepatitis B and the HPV vaccine it developed for the Indian market at a fraction of the imported price. One family firm in Pune is a load-bearing part of global immunisation, which is a concentration nobody chose and few discuss.

-71.06000,42.35500.name: Institute for Clinical and Economic Review
-71.06000,42.35500.desc: An independent US body that assesses whether a treatment's price is justified by its benefit, and has published on gene therapies priced in the millions. It has no legal power at all; its reports are used in negotiations because nobody else publishes the analysis, which makes a small non-profit a de facto price reference in a country with no formal one.

116.30000,40.04700.name: Novogene
116.30000,40.04700.desc: One of the highest-volume sequencing service providers in the world, reading samples sent from laboratories that do not own machines. Service sequencing means a great deal of the world's genetic data is generated in a handful of facilities in a small number of countries, whatever the sample's origin.
